fieldValues.title: A dead-issue-citation allowlist is a recurring shape, not a one-off — check every sibling before adding a third instance
fieldValues.summary: Two allowlist files in this repo (publication-reachability-exclusions.json, #590; integration-allowlist.json, #591) turned out to have the identical defect: an entry citing a GitHub issue whose closure is ambiguous between "settled ruling" and "dead follow-up pointer", fixed the same way both times — a required disposition field ("permanent" | "pending"). #427 (idl-schema-conformance-allowlist carries entries for deleted properties — the self-expiring-exception rule is not enforced) names a third allowlist with the same self-expiring-exception shape and is still open. Before authoring a bespoke fix for #427, check whether it is this same defect and the same disposition pattern applies directly.
fieldValues.rationale:
The Conformance cell's standing preference is "one way over many" (rfc-decision-cce3c00e). Two independent allowlists needing the identical schema addition is itself evidence this is one recurring shape, not two coincidences — so a third instance should default to reusing the pattern (disposition: permanent|pending, validated in the check script, proved red-then-green in tests/guards/run.mjs) rather than a new bespoke mechanism, unless #427's own shape turns out to differ (e.g. no natural open/closed issue citation to key off of).

What would change this: if #427's allowlist entries don't cite a tracking issue at all (they key on deleted schema properties, not GitHub issues per the title) — worth checking before assuming the pattern transfers verbatim; it may need a different discriminator (e.g. "property still absent from the schema" instead of issue state).
